meta.prompt: You are a worldclass math professor with expertise in breaking down math problems into easy to understand, coherent step

steps.title: Understand the Problem
steps.description:
We have a **regular hexagon** $ABCDEF$ with side length $15$ units. A regular hexagon means all 6 sides are equal and all 6 interior angles are equal.

**Part (a)** asks for the total distance around the shape — the perimeter.
**Part (b)** asks for each interior angle using a given formula.
**Part (c)** asks what happens when we draw the three main (long) diagonals — the diagonals that connect opposite vertices.

The key insight for part (c): a regular hexagon is secretly made of **6 equilateral triangles** — every side of those inner triangles equals the side length of the hexagon itself.

steps.title: Part (a): Find the Perimeter
steps.description:
The **perimeter** of any polygon is the sum of all its side lengths. Because all 6 sides of a regular hexagon are equal:

$$P = 6 \times \text{side length} = 6 \times 15 = 90 \text{ units}$$

steps.title: Part (b): Apply the Interior Angle Formula
steps.description:
The formula for each interior angle of a regular $n$-gon is:
$$\frac{(n-2) \cdot 180°}{n}$$

A hexagon has $n = 6$ sides. Substituting:
$$\frac{(6-2) \cdot 180°}{6} = \frac{4 \cdot 180°}{6} = \frac{720°}{6} = 120°$$

Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is $120°$. Notice that $720°$ is the **total interior angle sum** — dividing by $6$ gives the equal share for each vertex.

steps.title: Part (c): Count the Triangles
steps.description:
The **three main diagonals** connect opposite vertex pairs: $AD$, $BE$, and $CF$. These all intersect at the center point $O$, slicing the hexagon into $6$ triangular wedges.

Each wedge has:
- Two sides that are **radii** from the center to a vertex (equal in length to the side of the hexagon — a special property of regular hexagons)
- One side that is a **side of the hexagon** ($= 15$ units)

Because all three sides of every wedge are equal to $15$ units, each triangle is **equilateral**.

$$\text{Number of equilateral triangles} = 6, \quad \text{side length of each} = 15 \text{ units}$$

response.final_answer:
**(a)** $P = 6 \times 15 = \boxed{90}$ units

**(b)** $\dfrac{(6-2)\cdot 180°}{6} = \dfrac{720°}{6} = \boxed{120°}$ per interior angle

**(c)** The three main diagonals form $\boxed{6}$ equilateral triangles, each with side length $\boxed{15}$ units
